Jeremiah 1:5 “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; before you were born, I sanctified you; and I ordained you a prophet to the nations.“ Which yeah, refers to Jeremiah...just Jeremiah. One would think that the good Lord would have clued the Hebrews in if it applies to anyone else so they could make their laws in keeping with his. Unfortunately that doesn't appear to be the case since Numbers 5:11-31 describes how if a woman is suspected of adultery they will attempt to kill the fetus as a proof. Does that mesh with the sanctity of life? To kill an unborn child as a virtue test for the mother? However it is Biblical. Then there is good old Deuteronomy 19:21 which describes justice as a life for a life. If you kill a person you forfeit your life. Pretty much a societal standard world wide for centuries. Makes it very clear where the law and the good Lord stands on that.Then you have old problematic Exodus 21:22-25 which says if a man strikes a woman while he is fighting another man and causes her to miscarry then he has to pay a fine, but if the woman is further harmed then it goes back to old Deuteronomy.
While some will argue particular pedantic translation errors about whether yasa means a premature healthy birth or a miscarriage that point is immaterial when put alongside Numbers where a priest, the representative and conduit to the Lord prior to the tearing the veil, deliberately administers the bitter waters. Supposedly if the woman was unfaithful her womb would miscarry and her belly would swell. Now it is also important to note that this isn't just Moses telling the priesthood some stuff, this supposedly came straight from the Lord himself. So God Biblically supported and encouraged abortion in that particular circumstance and yet not one other place in the Bible is the killing of an unborn child ever mentioned as a sin or as a murder. Further, the fact that early translators chose miscarriage over premature birth indicates that early societies also did not see fetuses as people.
